Card 1 [ada-card-runner]
BRIEF: Tony idea 2026-11-12: an ada-tool that selects a kanban card by strategy (sweep, high-value, stale, queue), assembles just-enough context, launches an OpenChamber/opencode session with it, and evaluates until deployed to production.

Pilot: audit-drift cards — audit-hosts.py findings are already small, verifiable, card-shaped (declare-or-fix a unit, done-condition machine-checkable via systemctl/health). Card 5 [ada-memory-staged-writes]
BRIEF: Today any identity's memory save lands directly in a bank, and "I saved it" can be claimed without a write happening. This adds a staging lane: writes from guests/untrusted identities park in a pending collection until approved, while trusted identities keep writing directly — the write_approval pattern from Hermes, scoped by our existing access map.
SPEC: Where: ada-pi repo — tool_runner/memory.py write paths + a small pending store (MDDB collection ada-ha-memory-pending, or a vault pending/ dir — pick one, document in ssot.apps.ada-memory-banks.yml).  Routing rule — reuse the existing access map, don't invent a new ACL:   - person_policies {full: true} identities -> direct write (today's     behavior; Tony must not start approving every "remember X")   - restricted/unknown/guest identities -> staged   - per-bank write_policy: confirmed already gates the WRITE TOOL call;     staging gates the CONTENT for untrusted callers — complementary,     keep both.  Pending entry shape: {id, identity, bank, key, text, staged_at, source_session}. Approval applies the pinned content — if it changed after staging, refuse and keep pending (Hermes' pinning rule).  Approver surface: reuse an existing one — card comms + a board-api respond, or a nightly digest in focus-inbox. Do NOT build new UI.  Ada-visible behavior: model gets {ok: true, staged: true, id} and says "I'll keep that for Tony to approve" — never "saved".  Depends on ada-memory-injection-scan being the first line of defense; stage AFTER scanning, not before.
